newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 1.3 pct to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 1.3 pct to 11.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 1.3 percent to 11.3 percent on Friday, boosted by a higher volume of term loans.
Daily settlements totalled 67.7 million kuna ($10.8 million), against 107.7 million in supply. Call money, flat at 8.0 percent, accounted for half of the trade.
Creditors rolled over 30-day interbank money at an unchanged 15-percent rate, charging savings banks 17 and 18 percent for the same period.
One- and two-week interbank money went at 10 and 12 percent, respectively.
Insurers charged 12 percent for one-month loans, but savings banks and other financial institutions were paying 13 and 17 percent.
The central bank's kuna midrates were slightly firmer at 6.2619 against the dollar and at 3.5656 versus the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075 ($ = 6.242 Croatian Kuna)
